resources.string:
The passport details don't match the chip.

Please check:
• Passport number, exactly as printed, with no spaces
• Date of birth, in YYMMDD order
• Expiry date, in YYMMDD order

These are the two rows at the bottom of the photo page, not the dates printed above them.

Could not authenticate with the passport chip.

This could be caused by:
• A damaged or worn passport chip
• Interference during reading
• A protective case blocking the NFC signal

Try again with the phone on the passport cover, keeping it very steady.

PACE authentication failed.

This passport requires PACE before the chip data can be read.
• Check that the passport number, date of birth and expiry date match the MRZ exactly.
• If they are correct, this device may not support the chip or its security settings.

Keep the phone steady on the passport and try again, or try a different device if the problem persists.

PACE authentication failed at step %1$d.

This passport requires PACE before the chip data can be read.
• Check that the passport number, date of birth and expiry date match the MRZ exactly.
• If they are correct, this device may not support the chip or its security settings.

Keep the phone steady on the passport and try again, or try a different device if the problem persists.

Lift the phone off the passport, select Try again, then rest it back down. That refreshes the connection.

The order matters. Selecting Try again with the phone still on the passport tends to fail again, because the chip has to be found fresh.

If it keeps happening:
• Keep the phone still once it is down
• Remove any phone case or cover
• Keep both off metal surfaces

Something went wrong talking to the passport chip.

Lift the phone off the passport, select Try again, then rest it back down.

Things to try:
• Check NFC is switched on
• Take off any phone case
• Try a different position on the passport cover
• Check the passport chip is not damaged

Something went wrong talking to the passport chip.

Lift the phone off the passport, select Try again, then rest it back down.

%1$s

Things to try:
• Check NFC is switched on
• Take off any phone case
• Try a different position on the passport cover
• Check the passport chip is not damaged

Could not find the chip.

Things to try:
• Move the phone - front cover, back cover, then the photo page
• Take off any phone case, especially one with card slots or a magnet
• Take the passport out of any RFID-blocking wallet
• Check NFC is switched on

Could not verify that the passport is genuine.

This could mean:
• The certificate chain could not be validated
• The passport's digital signature is invalid
• The trust certificates are missing or out of date

The passport data was read, but it could not be confirmed as genuine.
Something unexpected went wrong while reading the passport.\n\nPlease try again.

Something unexpected went wrong while reading the passport.

%1$s

Please try again.
